I’ll ground this round-1 implementation review in the Project Source, start with the agenda, use the requested section structure, and focus on Git-managed issues, volume, and archive/compression impacts.

AGENDA  Should issues live inside Git-managed repo paths at all? — policy-rule-change candidate. The policy currently allows repo ledgers under issues/*.jsonl, but the discussion purpose explicitly includes avoiding misleading gates and unbounded repo bloat.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  If issues stay in Git, what belongs in Git and what should be outside Git? — evidence storage/retention task. My starting split: keep small, durable coordination records in Git; keep bulky evidence outside Git with stable refs, hashes, retention metadata, and retrieval instructions.  Does append-only JSONL make repo volume grow too much over time? — policy-rule-change candidate. Append-only is good for auditability, but the policy needs a bounded-growth model: active ledger, archived ledger, compacted index, and external evidence tiers.  Are large evidence files, raw CDP logs, source snapshots, bundles, and thread readbacks acceptable inside the repo? — evidence storage/retention task. Default answer: no, not in the normal working tree unless explicitly small, sanitized, and needed for day-to-day reproducibility.  If compression, sharding, archive branches, git-annex/LFS, artifact stores, or periodic compaction exist, do they remove the concern or only move it? — policy-rule-change candidate. They mostly move the concern unless policy defines ownership, retention class, integrity verification, discoverability, and worker recovery behavior.  Should issues/*.jsonl mean all files must be current issue.record.v1, or should legacy files be excluded by name/path/schema? — tooling/gate task. Current ops reality shows a full gate over ops/issues/*.jsonl fails on legacy 260519.jsonl, while a scoped current-v1 chain passes.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Should validation always cover all issues/*.jsonl, or should there be separate gates for full repo, active chain, migration, and release? — tooling/gate task. There should be multiple gates with explicit meanings; “everything under glob” is too blunt for repos with legacy history.  Should repo-specific issue design be allowed, or must policy impose one cross-repo issue schema? — policy-rule-change candidate. Policy should impose a minimal interoperable interface, not a complete universal schema.  Should policy define a minimal issue interface and let repos own richer local issue schemas? — policy-rule-change candidate. Yes. Required fields should support worker start, review, recovery, and merge hygiene; repo-local fields should be allowed when namespaced or declared.  How should blocked be defined so it does not get confused with “tool cannot be used at all”? — policy-rule-change candidate. blocked should mean the issue cannot progress under its current close criteria until a named blocker is resolved, not that the affected subsystem or tool is globally unusable.  How should a large issue be narrowed after partial resolution without pretending it is closed? — repo-local issue design change candidate. Use same issueId with a superseding record when the issue identity remains the same but scope narrows; record resolved subclaims and remaining close criteria.  When should issue updates use same issueId with supersedes, and when should they split into a new issue? — policy-rule-change candidate. Same issue when the worker-facing problem and close criteria remain continuous; split when ownership, allowed paths, target repo, risk class, or close criteria diverge.  Should evidence stay as small string refs, or move to structured evidenceRefs[] with hashes, sizes, retention class, and storage tier? — policy-rule-change candidate. Move to structured evidence refs. This is central to handling large evidence without making the repo the artifact store.  How should old legacy JSONL like 260519.jsonl be migrated, quarantined, or grandfathered? — migration/backfill task. Quarantine by path or schema first; then optionally backfill a v1 index record that points to the legacy record as evidence.  What invariant must hold so a worker can start from one latest issue record plus repo policy? — policy-rule-change candidate. The latest active record must include enough target, scope, allowed paths, status, close criteria, blocker, evidence refs, and handoff context for safe continuation; the current policy already requires many of these fields.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Should active issue ledgers and archived issue ledgers use separate paths? — repo-local issue design change candidate. Yes: e.g. issues/active/*.jsonl, issues/archive/*.jsonl, issues/legacy/*.jsonl, or a repo-local equivalent.  Should full-history validation be required for normal worker startup? — tooling/gate task. No. Normal workers need active-chain validity plus evidence ref reachability; release or migration jobs can run full-history validation.  Should policy require explicit schema version detection rather than relying on file glob meaning? — policy-rule-change candidate. Yes. A record-level schemaVersion or kind discriminator prevents old files from poisoning current gates.  Should issue records include evidence retention and privacy/sensitivity class? — evidence storage/retention task. Yes. Raw browser logs, source snapshots, and thread readbacks can contain secrets, private text, or large duplicate content.  Should compaction create a new authoritative latest record or a derived index? — policy-rule-change candidate. It should create a derived index unless explicitly reviewed as a superseding authoritative record; otherwise compaction risks rewriting the audit trail.  Should merge conflict hygiene be part of issue-ledger design? — repo-local issue design change candidate. Yes. Daily shards reduce conflicts but increase cross-shard validation complexity; per-issue files reduce line conflicts but may weaken append-only chronology.  Should issue IDs be globally unique, repo-scoped, or branch-scoped? — policy-rule-change candidate. They should be repo-scoped at minimum, with enough namespace to avoid collision during cross-repo handoff.  Should Markdown issue files remain “legacy evidence” by default? — no-change-needed, with one caveat: the policy should require tooling to ignore them for machine issue gates unless explicitly opted in. The source notes Markdown issue files are currently legacy evidence, but ops still has them under ops/issues/.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Should the policy distinguish issue state from external tool state? — policy-rule-change candidate. Yes. This is the blocked confusion in broader form: an issue can be blocked while the repo, Project Source, ChatGPT thread, or local tool remains partially usable.  POSITION  Recommended direction: keep a Git-managed issue interface, but stop treating Git as the universal issue/evidence database.  The policy should require a small, durable, machine-readable issue ledger that is good enough for worker startup, review, merge, and recovery. It should not require every repo to place all historical issues, all evidence, and all local issue detail under one active issues/*.jsonl gate. The current snapshot says issue queues use JSONL, each line is a complete issue.record.v1, updates repeat issueId with supersedes, and validation currently targets the complete issues/*.jsonl set because supersedes must resolve.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   That is coherent for a clean new repo, but brittle for a real repo with legacy records, Markdown evidence, large artifacts, and evolving local workflows.  My B-style challenge to likely A-style assumptions: do not assume that “more process in Git” automatically improves recoverability. A single strict full-ledger gate can become a false authority: it may fail because of harmless legacy files, pass while evidence is missing, or encourage teams to stuff huge artifacts into Git just to satisfy review rituals. The better invariant is: a worker can safely start from the latest active issue record plus repo policy, and a reviewer can verify the issue’s evidence refs without needing the entire artifact history in the working tree.  I would change policy in three places: define a minimal cross-repo issue interface, define active/archive/legacy validation classes, and replace unstructured evidence strings with structured evidenceRefs[]. I would leave richer local issue schemas to repo policy, provided they project down to the minimal interface.  POLICY_GAPS  issues/*.jsonl is overloaded. It currently appears to mean “all issue ledger files,” “all current v1 issue records,” and “the complete validation universe.” Ops shows that this breaks when a legacy JSONL file exists under the same glob. Full validation fails on 260519.jsonl, while the scoped v1 chain passes.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  No clear active/archive/legacy distinction. The policy says Markdown issue files are legacy evidence unless a command says otherwise, but it does not give an equally clear rule for legacy JSONL. That leaves 260519.jsonl in a bad middle state: too structured to ignore, too old to validate.  Evidence is underspecified. “Required evidence” is a useful worker field, but policy does not appear to define evidence size, storage tier, retention class, hash integrity, sensitivity, or expected availability. That is the main blind spot for raw CDP logs, source snapshots, bundles, and thread readbacks.  Append-only has no lifecycle. Append-only snapshots are good for audit, but policy needs archive and compaction semantics. Without them, a repo either bloats indefinitely or invents local cleanup practices that may silently weaken auditability.  blocked is too absolute. The current definition says work must not continue until the blocker is resolved.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   That is appropriate at issue scope, but it can be misread as “the tool/subsystem cannot be used at all.” Policy should say blocked is scoped to the issue record’s target, close criteria, allowed paths, and blocker.  No narrowing semantics. The Project Source issue was narrowed after live reproof succeeded, leaving a consistency issue between project-transport-env / project-source-list and worker-readable proof.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   Policy should explicitly support “partially resolved, narrowed, still open/ready” without pretending the old broad issue was simply closed.  No split-vs-supersede rule. The policy says later updates repeat issueId and list the previous recordId in supersedes, but it does not define when a changed scope deserves a new issue instead.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Validation is treated as one gate. The source says complete ledger validation is required because supersedes must resolve.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   That misses the operational need for separate active-chain, full-history, migration, and release gates.  Cross-repo schema may be too heavy. Required fields like target repo, branch, allowed paths, close criteria, required evidence, blocker, and handoff are valuable, but policy should avoid forcing every repo to abandon richer local schemas if they can expose the minimal interface.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  REPO_DESIGN_GAPS  Legacy JSONL sits in the active glob. ops/issues/260519.jsonl is legacy shape, not issue.record.v1, but it lives where the current full gate expects v1 records. That creates a deterministic false failure.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Current v1 chain is valid only by scoped selection. The chain 260524.jsonl + 260525.jsonl + 260526.jsonl passes when scoped.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   This suggests the repo already has an implicit active-chain concept, but the directory layout and validation commands do not encode it.  Markdown and evidence directories are mixed under ops/issues/. The policy treats Markdown issue files as legacy evidence unless a command says otherwise, but repo reality still places Markdown and evidence directories under the issue area.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   This makes it too easy for humans and tools to disagree about what is authoritative.  Evidence storage has no visible tier boundary. Large artifacts should not live beside active queue records unless explicitly classified. The repo needs at least: small refs in active records, local retained evidence for short-term review, and external/archive evidence for bulk artifacts.  Issue narrowing appears ad hoc. ops.project-source-worker-readable-upload was narrowed after reproof, but the repo needs a standard pattern for recording resolved subclaims, remaining claim, and why the same issue identity still applies.  Status semantics are not worker-proof. ready-for-work plus a narrowed issue is reasonable, but only if the latest record has sufficient close criteria and blocker semantics. Otherwise a worker may reopen solved parts or overgeneralize the remaining inconsistency.  Tooling bug issue is cleanly separate and should stay separate. ops.thread-fsm-marker-substring concerns NO_UNRESOLVED_OBJECTIONS being misclassified as an objection marker.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   That should not be bundled into broader Project Source transport issues.  MIGRATION_PLAN  Freeze current layout behavior. Do not rewrite existing legacy files in place. Record that 260519.jsonl is legacy evidence, not active v1 ledger input.  Introduce explicit paths or manifest. Prefer paths such as:  issues/active/*.jsonl for current issue.record.v1  issues/archive/*.jsonl for valid old v1 closed/superseded chains  issues/legacy/*.jsonl for non-v1 historical JSONL  issues/evidence/ only for small retained evidence, with size and retention rules  If path movement is too disruptive, add an issues/ledger-manifest.json that declares active, archive, legacy, and evidence inputs.  Quarantine 260519.jsonl without rewriting its content. Move it to a legacy path in a normal Git commit, or leave it in place and exclude it through a manifest. Add one v1 “legacy-index” or “migration-note” record that points to it as evidence and explains why it is not part of active v1 validation.  Keep the passing current chain intact. Treat 260524.jsonl + 260525.jsonl + 260526.jsonl as the active v1 chain for now, since the source says that scoped gate already passes.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Add structured evidence refs going forward. New or superseding records should use evidenceRefs[] with at least: ref, kind, sha256 where available, sizeBytes where available, storageTier, retentionClass, sensitivity, and requiredForClose.  Define validation modes before broad migration.  active: validates active v1 chain and latest-record worker invariant.  full-v1: validates all declared v1 ledgers and cross-ledger supersedes.  legacy-inventory: checks legacy files are named, classified, and referenced.  release: combines active, full-v1, evidence reachability, and no unexpected files under active paths.  migration: permits known legacy exceptions but fails on new unclassified ones.  Backfill only indexes, not history. For old Markdown or legacy JSONL, create small v1 index records that preserve provenance and point to original artifacts. Do not mutate old records just to make them look native.  Document split/supersede local rules. Ops should add a short repo-local issue policy: when to narrow, when to split, how to record partial resolution, and where evidence should live.  RISKS  Repo bloat. Keeping raw logs, bundles, source snapshots, and readbacks in Git will eventually harm clone time, review ergonomics, and merge hygiene. Compression may reduce size but not governance burden.  Archive solutions can hide evidence. LFS, git-annex, artifact stores, and archive branches can preserve blobs while making them unavailable to a worker. The policy must require stable refs, hashes, and retrieval expectations.  Validation false positives. A full issues/*.jsonl gate currently fails on known legacy shape. That is a false positive for active work if the active v1 chain is valid.  Validation false negatives. A scoped active-chain gate may pass while archived supersedes are broken, evidence refs are missing, or legacy records contain unresolved obligations. That is why separate gate classes are needed.  Worker usability drift. If latest records depend on tribal knowledge, old Markdown, or bulky unindexed artifacts, workers cannot safely start from one issue record plus repo policy.  Merge conflicts. Append-only JSONL improves auditability but can cause frequent same-file conflicts if many actors update the same shard. Sharding helps but complicates supersedes resolution.  Misleading closure. Without narrowing semantics, teams may close a broad issue after solving one major subclaim, leaving residual inconsistency untracked.  Status overgeneralization. blocked can be misread as global tool failure. That can stop unrelated progress or create exaggerated incident records.  Schema rigidity. A single universal schema may force local repos into awkward workarounds. Conversely, no minimal interface makes cross-repo handoff and review unreliable.  Evidence sensitivity. Raw CDP logs and thread readbacks may include secrets, private data, or prompt/source material that should not be committed to ordinary repo history.  OPEN_QUESTIONS  Should the peer thread accept the principle that Git holds the issue control plane, not the evidence data plane?  Should issues/*.jsonl be deprecated as an active-ledger glob in favor of issues/active/*.jsonl, or should a manifest be preferred to avoid path churn?  What is the minimum issue.record.v1 interface that every repo must expose: latest status, target, branch, allowed paths, close criteria, blocker, handoff, and structured evidence refs?  Should legacy JSONL be allowed under issues/ at all, or must all legacy records move under issues/legacy/?  Should compaction be allowed to create authoritative superseding records, or only derived indexes?  What size threshold should force evidence out of normal Git? For example, should anything over a small fixed size require storageTier != git-working-tree?  How should a worker behave when an evidence ref is unavailable but not marked requiredForClose?  Should a release gate require all archived evidence to be reachable, or only evidence required for active and recently closed issues?  Should blocked be renamed or supplemented with blockedScope to prevent global-tool misreadings?  Should the Project Source consistency issue remain a narrowed same-issueId record, or should disagreement between project-transport-env / project-source-list and worker-readable proof become a new issue?  Should the NO_UNRESOLVED_OBJECTIONS marker bug be used as a test case for split-vs-supersede rules?  Should policy require repo-local issue design docs to define active paths, archive paths, evidence tiers, validation modes, and split/narrowing rules before a repo can claim compliance?  Should the “same proposalRevision no-objections before pass” rule remain purely discussion-process policy, or should issue ledgers encode discussion state as evidence refs rather than status gates? The Project Source notes that facilitator summary is not a verdict and same-revision no-objections are required before pass.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  What is the recovery invariant for a fresh clone with no artifact-store credentials: should it be able to list active work only, verify active work, or fully reproduce evidence?  How should peer review challenge A-style assumptions that “full validation over every historical file” equals safety, when current ops evidence shows scoped active validation can be meaningful while full glob validation is blocked by legacy format?   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…

I’ll compare B’s reply against A’s prior position and the original discussion scope, separating strongest points, objections, agenda changes, disposition, and unresolved issues without claiming approval.

PEER_REVIEW 1. Strongest points from B  B’s strongest contribution is the invariant-vs-HOWTO distinction. I agree that global policy should define authority, provenance, replayability, validation boundaries, archive integrity, approval boundaries, and backend declarations, while repo-local design should own concrete storage choices, compression mechanics, SQLite/materialized views, and runtime adapters. That sharpens A’s “minimal interface, repo-local richer schema” position rather than replacing it.   THREAD_B_REPLY_V1  B also adds a needed concurrency dimension. A focused on bloat, legacy glob failure, evidence refs, and validation modes; B correctly says Git-managed issues are only safe if the repo declares whether it is single-writer, multi-writer, or hybrid. That is a real blind spot in A: issues/*.jsonl can be append-only and still suffer same-issue contention around status, ownership, dependencies, closure, or blocker fields.  B’s approval-boundary point is important and should be adopted. File upload, readback, thread reply, generated report, branch inventory, or issue-ledger record should not by themselves authorize merge, push, cleanup, branch deletion, issue closure, or implementation acceptance. This aligns with the Project Source rule that facilitator summary is not a verdict and same-proposalRevision no-objections are required before pass.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  B’s event/replay/snapshot/archive framing is a useful escalation path for large volume. The current policy snapshot says issue queues use JSONL, each line is a complete issue.record.v1 snapshot, later lines update by repeating issueId with supersedes, and validation currently targets the complete ledger set because supersedes must resolve.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   B is right that, at scale, raw log scans should not be the normal read path; there should be a replayable canonical source plus derived latest-state views, snapshots, segment manifests, and cold archive verification.  B’s generated-view point should be accepted. Markdown issue pages, dashboards, summaries, and review packets should be disposable views, not canonical issue state. That reinforces A’s concern that Markdown/evidence directories under ops/issues/ blur machine authority and legacy evidence. The Project Source notes that Markdown issue files are legacy evidence by policy, while repo reality still includes Markdown and evidence directories under ops/issues/.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  B’s post-publish divergence risk is worth adding. A emphasized validation false positives and false negatives. B adds the concrete risk that code state and issue state can diverge after publish unless remote state is compared. Even if refs/issues are not the current canonical shape, the agenda item should generalize to “atomicity or post-publish verification for code + issue state.”  2. Objections to B  First, B did not fully satisfy the original round-1 shape. The Project Source required agenda enumeration and classification across the named topics, including Git-managed issue location, evidence boundaries, append-only volume, compression/archive, legacy JSONL, validation modes, repo-specific schema, blocked, narrowing, split-vs-supersede, structured evidence refs, legacy migration, and worker-start invariant.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   B’s agenda is a compact paragraph, not a numbered classified agenda. That is a format and process gap, even though its substance is useful.  Second, B’s opening source-boundary caveat weakens its authority. B says it treated ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_V1.md as controlling but did not retrieve the exact verbatim file.   THREAD_B_REPLY_V1   In this peer review, the controlling file is available and shows concrete current-policy and ops-repo facts, including 260519.jsonl legacy shape, full gate failure, scoped current-v1 success, the narrowed Project Source issue, the NO_UNRESOLVED_OBJECTIONS marker bug, and mixed Markdown/evidence directories.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   B’s architectural objections should be retained, but its review should be considered revision input, not a directly sufficient peer signoff.  Third, B may overcorrect from “Git issue ledger has gaps” to “event-sourced platform redesign.” The current policy is snapshot-based: each JSONL line is a complete issue.record.v1, with updates via issueId and supersedes.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…   B’s proposed event schema, replay layer, source-artifact ledger, snapshots, cold archive lifecycle, fsck suite, and generated outputs may be right for scaled repos, but they are not a minimal patch. This is a repo-local design track plus possibly a later policy track, not something to fold wholesale into v1.  Fourth, B under-addresses several immediate A/source issues: legacy JSONL quarantine, active/archive/legacy path or manifest, scoped active-chain validation, blocked scope, issue narrowing, split-vs-supersede criteria, and the current ops issues. A specifically proposed a control-plane/data-plane split, active/archive/legacy validation classes, and structured evidenceRefs[], while preserving richer repo-local schema.   THREAD_A_REPLY_V1   B’s event model should not displace those immediate fixes.  Fifth, B’s evidence-state taxonomy is directionally correct but may be too broad for the issue-ledger policy itself. raw_evidence, candidate_summary, adopted_policy, rejected, deprecated, hold, and out_of_scope are useful, but some belong to Project Source artifact governance or discussion policy rather than every issue record. The policy patch should require source/evidence classification hooks; repo-local design can choose the full taxonomy.  Sixth, B relies on adjacent artifacts such as ticket-vs-Beads, JSONL+SQLite PoC, snapshot lifecycle, runtime boundary, and worst-case simulations. Those are useful supporting evidence, but the peer-review decision for this discussion should distinguish “direct Project Source facts” from “adjacent design evidence.” Otherwise policy can be captured by implementation-specific examples.  3. Agenda items to add/remove/rename  Add:  Issue backend/concurrency mode — policy-rule-change candidate. Each repo should declare single-writer, multi-writer, or hybrid semantics, including CAS/claim rules for status, ownership, dependency, blocker, and closure fields.  Event stream vs complete snapshot model — policy-rule-change candidate. The current policy is complete issue.record.v1 snapshots with supersedes; B proposes event streams. The agenda must decide whether v1 stays snapshot-based, moves event-based, or permits both behind a minimal interface.  Approval boundary — policy-rule-change candidate. Explicitly state that artifact existence, issue records, generated reports, summaries, and readbacks are evidence, not approval.  Generated views are non-authoritative — repo-local issue design change candidate. Markdown pages, dashboards, latest SQLite, and review packets must be rebuildable and disposable unless explicitly promoted.  Latest-state materialization threshold — repo-local issue design/tooling-gate task. Define when a repo may or must stop scanning raw JSONL for ordinary reads and use a derived latest-state view.  Replay/fsck/idempotence requirements — tooling/gate task. Add deterministic replay, duplicate-event/idempotency behavior, missing-parent/supersedes checks, evidence hash checks, and generated-view rebuild checks.  Snapshot/segment/cold archive lifecycle — evidence storage/retention task. Compression should be governed by manifest, hash, restore, and replay boundaries, not merely file size.  Code-state/issue-state publication consistency — tooling/gate task. Decide whether atomic publication is required or whether post-push compare-and-repair is acceptable.  Source/evidence state taxonomy — policy-rule-change candidate, but with scope control. Require classification; do not necessarily mandate B’s full vocabulary globally.  Policy-vs-runbook boundary — policy-rule-change candidate. Prevent global policy from absorbing package, WebMCP, CDP, forge, SQLite, or shell HOWTO details.  Rename:  Rename “Should issues live inside Git-managed repo paths at all?” to “Should Git hold the issue control plane, the evidence data plane, or both?”  Rename “Does append-only JSONL make repo volume grow too much?” to “How do append-only audit logs combine with materialized latest views, snapshots, and cold archive?”  Rename “If compression/archive exists, does it remove the concern?” to “What archive lifecycle preserves issue meaning, evidence integrity, and replay?”  Rename “Should validation cover all issues/*.jsonl?” to “What validation mode applies: active, full-v1/full-replay, migration, release, or archive-restore?”  Rename “Should repo-specific issue design be allowed?” to “What global issue interface must repo-local backends project to?”  Rename “How should blocked be defined?” to “What is the scope and authority boundary of issue status values?”  Rename “When use same issueId/supersedes vs split?” to “What are the mutation semantics for narrowing, supersession, split, reopen, and event/snapshot transition?”  Remove or demote:  Do not remove any of the original fifteen required agenda topics. Demote implementation-specific examples—SQLite, Beads/Dolt, refs/issues, gzip/zstd, WebMCP, package-specific commands—from global policy agenda to repo-local design evidence unless the policy text only uses them as non-normative examples.  4. Disposition of v1  v1 should not become a direct implementation-ready policy patch. It should become a split work package:  Policy patch seed: control-plane/data-plane split; minimal issue interface; structured evidence/source refs; evidence classification; approval boundary; schema/path/manifest declaration; validation modes; blocked scope; split/narrow/supersede rules; archive integrity invariants; backend mode declaration.  Repo-local design task: choose ops issue backend mode; define active/archive/legacy paths or manifest; decide whether to remain snapshot JSONL or add event-stream projection; define latest-state materialization; define generated views; define archive storage; define post-publish verification.  Migration task: quarantine or manifest-exclude 260519.jsonl; preserve it as legacy evidence; keep the passing 260524 + 260525 + 260526 current-v1 chain intact; inventory Markdown/evidence directories; add migration/index records without rewriting legacy history. The source shows the legacy file fails the full glob gate while the scoped current-v1 chain passes.   ISSUE_LEDGER_POLICY_DISCUSSION_…  Discussion-only for now: event-sourced canonical model, SQLite/latest-state thresholds, cold archive restore SLA, same-issue multi-agent mutation semantics, and atomic issue/code publication. These need further decision before policy wording becomes mandatory.
